log.headline: 56 points, +6 on the 50-point average. Overall rank 2,677,591.
notes: Vuskovic (0 Premier League minutes, behind Kadioglu, Struijk and Dunk at Brighton) replaced by Luke Shaw, who started all 38 last season.
Gvardiol (16 starts, heavily rotated) replaced by Marc Guehi (35 starts, 179 points) - same club, same fixture, far more certain minutes.
Net cost GBP 0.0m: the GBP 0.5m saved on Shaw paid for the Guehi upgrade exactly.
No chip played. Nothing to gain in GW1 and the bench is worth roughly 2 points on a Bench Boost.

RESULT: João Pedro 11 (goal, assist, 2 bonus), Guéhi 10 (goal, 2 bonus), Calafiori 9 (assist, clean sheet), Szoboszlai 8 (goal, 1 bonus). Haaland captained for 2 points, doubled to 4 — 90 minutes, 0.74 xG, no return.
7 points left on the bench, 6 of them Slater's (assist plus clean sheet at Hull) — the single biggest avoidable loss of the week.

The Guéhi swap paid off, but not for the reason given. He was advised on his Crystal Palace starts record, which was the wrong evidence. He delivered because Maresca is reportedly playing him in central midfield, a role change nobody predicted here.
The Shaw swap looks flat so far: 90 minutes, 1 point, 2 goals conceded — but the reasoning (guaranteed minutes over a player with none) still holds.

log.headline: 95 points, +14 on the 81-point average. Overall rank climbed 803,799 places to 1,873,792 - top 25%.
notes: Haaland delivered this time: 2 goals, 13 raw / 26 with the armband, at Crystal Palace. The GW1 blank really was fatigue, not lost form.

Bruno Fernandes had the bigger raw game (23 points - a hat-trick plus an assist, 3 bonus, at home to Ipswich under new manager Michael Carrick) than Haaland's 13. The captaincy call still went to Haaland on underlying + fixture logic and it worked, but Bruno's score shows the alternative case wasn't wrong, just lower-ceiling this particular week.
Guéhi reverted to orthodox centre-back (no repeat of the GW1 midfield cameo) in a 4-1 win over his old club Crystal Palace - 2 points, appearance only, no clean sheet, no goal involvement this time.
Calafiori (11: assist + clean sheet) and Raya (6: clean sheet) both delivered as Arsenal won away at Aston Villa without conceding.
Liverpool conceded twice at home to Forest: Virgil 1 point, Szoboszlai 4. Neither is an emergency after one bad defensive day, but both are now on the watch list.
Shaw played 72 minutes and returned only 2 points - the underlying weakness flagged pre-match (thin defensive-contribution numbers) played out as expected.
4 points left on the bench (down from 7 in GW1) - the Slater-to-front bench reorder advised last week worked.
No transfers made. 1 free transfer rolled into GW3 alongside a second - 2 FT banked, still no hits taken all season.

log.headline: 62 points, +11 on the 51-point average. Overall rank climbed 787,212 to 1,086,580 - top 20% on the gameweek.
notes: Triple Captain on Haaland paid off: 9 raw (1 goal, 3 bonus, clean sheet involvement) tripled to 27 - the single biggest score of the season so far.
Shaw-to-Egan worked immediately: Egan started all 90, kept a clean sheet, 6 points at £4.0m. Shaw would have played the same fixture shape at Everton; the swap was pure upgrade.

Guéhi (8, clean sheet + 2 bonus) and Virgil (6, clean sheet) both delivered on kind fixtures (Coventry H, Ipswich A) exactly as backed - Virgil in particular did not blank, clearing last week's 'sell if he blanks again' trigger.
Bruno Fernandes and João Pedro both quiet by their standards (2 and 1 point) - the vice-captaincy on Bruno wasn't needed since Haaland played and scored.
7 points left on the bench again - Slater (3, clean sheet) the biggest miss, same pattern as GW1. Bench order held Slater in front all week; the value just wasn't reachable without a Bench Boost.
No hits taken all season, 0 points lost to transfer costs.

log.headline: 89 points, +20 on the 69-point average. Overall rank climbed 442,363 to 644,217 - top 6% on the gameweek.
notes: Captain João Pedro delivered exactly as backed: goal, assist, 3 bonus - 12 raw doubled to 24, the single biggest armband return of the season so far.

Man City won 1-0 away at Man Utd in the derby: Haaland (9: goal, clean sheet, 3 bonus), Guéhi (6: clean sheet) and Anderson (5: clean sheet) all profited - the tough fixture that nearly kept the armband on Haaland turned out fine for him anyway, just not as the captain.
Calvert-Lewin's best game yet: goal, assist, clean sheet, 2 bonus for 10 points at Leeds in 77 minutes.
Raya's biggest week of the season: clean sheet plus 3 bonus for 14 points away at Sunderland.

Only 3 points left on the bench (down from 7 in GW3) - Slater (2) and Hughes (1, his first involvement of the season - 13 minutes off the bench) were the only bench scorers; Dubravka and van Ewijk blanked.
No transfers made, no hits taken all season.

log.headline: Hold. Captain Haaland (H v Sunderland) over João Pedro, whose knee knock stays unconfirmed past the deadline. Deadline Fri 18 Sep, 17:30 UTC.
notes: João Pedro (knee, 75% per the FPL API) picked up the knock in the GW4 win over Hull; Xabi Alonso gave no committal answer at Thursday's press conference. Brentford host Chelsea at 19:00 UTC Friday - after our deadline - so this is a blind call either way. Kept in the XI rather than sold: premierleague.com's own advice is 'keep, consider benching', and Calvert-Lewin is already rostered as cover if he blanks.

Captain switched to Haaland: home to newly-promoted Sunderland, four goals in his last three, still Man City's confirmed #1 penalty taker under Enzo Maresca, and the near-unanimous pick across RotoWire, Fantasy Football Hub and Fantasy Football Scout. Vice moves to Bruno Fernandes (nailed, Sunday fixture) rather than the doubtful João Pedro.

Anderson and Szoboszlai both reviewed as possible sells and both held: Anderson's recent withdrawal was confirmed as cramp, not injury, and he's tipped for growing set-piece duties at City; Szoboszlai's form dip is real (4.5) but a huge GW1 outlier is skewing the season number, not a genuine collapse, per allaboutfpl.com.
Bruno Fernandes is the single most transferred-out player in the game by count (218,301 this event) despite ranking 1st in the squad for expected goal involvement - held, not sold.

Will Hughes remains the clearest transfer target once a specific, verified replacement is found - zero starts in five gameweeks, though he did get his first minutes of the season (13, off the bench) in GW4. Stays last in the bench order, costing nothing.

Calafiori rose again to £5.8m (sells £5.6m) and João Pedro to £7.8m (sells £7.6m); Anderson fell to £6.3m and Hughes to £4.4m. Spending power £99.9m (£99.4m sell value + £0.5m bank). Calafiori, Raya, Guéhi and Haaland were all close to a further rise as of last night.
All chips held. No double gameweek and no injury crisis beyond a single day-to-day doubt that the squad already covers for free via the bench.

COULD NOT VERIFY: Daniel Muñoz's current club (named in one source as a defensive replacement, ambiguous); Szoboszlai's exact current fitness beyond the API's status='a' (only mismatched/ambiguous injury threads found) - both checked 17 Sep 2026.
